items.name: Data Protection Officer
items.summary: Establishes the DPO function required by GDPR Articles 37-39, ensuring ABC Insurance Group has an empowered, independent privacy authority overseeing all personal-data processing across its insurance lines.

subs.title: Designated, Resourced, and Independent DPO
subs.description: A Data Protection Officer is formally appointed with the expertise required by Article 37, given adequate budget, staff, and access to processing operations, and protected from instruction or dismissal for performing the role. The DPO must be consulted early on all matters involving personal data, including new underwriting models, claims platforms, and policyholder analytics, not brought in after decisions are made.

subs.title: DPO as Contact Point for Authority and Data Subjects
subs.description: The DPO's contact details are published in privacy notices and registered with the relevant supervisory authority, serving as the single point of contact for regulator inquiries and for policyholders, claimants, and beneficiaries exercising their rights. Inbound contacts are tracked and answered within defined service levels so no regulator or data-subject communication goes unhandled.

items.name: Data Protection by Design & by Default
items.summary: Privacy controls such as pseudonymisation, data minimisation, and access limits are embedded into system and process architecture from inception per GDPR Article 25, and every system defaults to its most privacy-protective configuration rather than relying on users to opt down. New policy administration, claims, and analytics builds must demonstrate these controls at design review, before any personal data is processed.

items.name: International Data Transfers
items.summary: Personal data may leave the EEA only under a valid GDPR Chapter V mechanism, namely an adequacy decision, Standard Contractual Clauses, or Binding Corporate Rules, supported by a documented transfer impact assessment and supplementary measures such as encryption where the destination's legal regime requires them post-Schrems II. This governs transfers to offshore claims processing, reinsurers, and group entities, and undocumented transfer routes are treated as compliance violations.

items.name: Lawful Basis for Processing
items.summary: Governs the legal justification for every use of personal data under GDPR Article 6, ensuring no processing activity at ABC Insurance Group, from quoting and underwriting to claims and marketing, operates without a documented legal foundation that can be evidenced to a supervisory authority.

subs.title: Documented Article 6 Lawful Basis Before Collection
subs.description: Each processing activity is assigned exactly one Article 6 basis, whether consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests, and the determination is recorded in the processing register before any personal data is collected. The chosen basis constrains downstream rights handling, for example which activities are subject to erasure or objection, so it cannot be retrofitted after collection begins.

subs.title: Balancing Test for Legitimate Interests
subs.description: Where legitimate interests is the chosen basis, a documented Legitimate Interests Assessment must weigh the carrier's interest against the rights and reasonable expectations of policyholders and claimants, considering less intrusive alternatives. The assessment is approved by the privacy function, retained as evidence, and revisited when the processing or its context changes.

items.name: Personal Data Breach Notification
items.summary: Defines how personal-data breaches are detected, risk-assessed, and reported under GDPR Articles 33 and 34, so that ABC Insurance Group meets regulatory deadlines and affected policyholders are warned in time to protect themselves.

subs.title: Detection, Assessment, and 72-Hour Notification
subs.description: Security monitoring and incident response feed a privacy triage process that determines, for each confirmed breach, whether it poses a risk to individuals and therefore requires notification to the supervisory authority within 72 hours of awareness. Where the breach is likely to result in high risk, for example exposure of claims medical files or policyholder financial details, affected data subjects are informed without undue delay with clear guidance on protective steps.

subs.title: Breach Register Maintenance
subs.description: Every personal-data breach is logged in a register regardless of whether it met the notification threshold, recording the facts, effects, assessment rationale, and remedial action taken. The register is the evidence a supervisory authority will inspect to verify Article 33(5) compliance and is reviewed periodically for recurring root causes.

items.name: Processor & DPA Management
items.summary: Every processor and sub-processor handling personal data on the carrier's behalf, including TPAs, cloud providers, and claims-service vendors, must operate under an Article 28 data processing agreement that establishes a documented sub-processor authorisation chain, audit rights, and processing strictly on documented instructions. Vendor onboarding cannot complete, and data cannot flow, until the DPA is executed and recorded.

items.name: Purpose Limitation & Data Minimisation
items.summary: Enforces the GDPR Article 5 principles that personal data is collected for specified purposes and limited to what those purposes require, preventing the gradual accumulation of unjustified policyholder and claimant data across ABC Insurance Group's quoting, underwriting, and claims systems.

subs.title: Collect Only Data Necessary for the Stated Purpose
subs.description: Application forms, claims intake flows, and data feeds are scoped to the minimum personal data needed for the declared purpose, such as rating a policy or adjudicating a claim. Requests to capture additional data must demonstrate necessity for an approved purpose rather than convenience or speculative future value.

subs.title: Documented Purpose for Every Field
subs.description: Each personal-data field in a system's data model carries a recorded purpose in the data dictionary or processing register, traceable to a lawful processing activity. Fields whose purpose cannot be articulated are flagged for removal during periodic data-inventory reviews.

subs.title: Design Rejection of Purposeless Fields
subs.description: Architecture and design review gates refuse new schemas, forms, or integration contracts that introduce personal-data fields lacking a documented purpose. This makes minimisation a build-time control rather than an after-the-fact cleanup exercise.

subs.title: No Re-Use for Incompatible Purposes
subs.description: Personal data collected for one purpose, such as claims handling, may not be repurposed for an incompatible one, such as cross-line marketing or model training, without a compatibility assessment and, where required, a new lawful basis and updated notice. Downstream consumers including analytics and data-science teams are bound by the original purpose recorded against the data.

items.name: Records of Processing Activities (RoPA)
items.summary: A living Article 30 inventory documents every processing activity together with its purposes, data categories, recipients, international transfers, and retention periods, and is updated as systems and vendors change rather than rebuilt annually. The RoPA is the backbone for DSAR fulfilment, transfer governance, and breach assessment, so change management for insurance platforms must include a RoPA update step.

items.name: Restriction & Objection
items.summary: Article 18 processing-restriction flags and Article 21 objections, including the absolute right to opt out of direct marketing, are implemented as enforceable controls at the data layer rather than manual notes, so that batch jobs, analytics pipelines, and campaign systems automatically exclude restricted or objecting policyholders. Downstream processing that ignores these flags is treated as a control failure.

items.name: Right of Access (DSAR)
items.summary: Implements the GDPR Article 15 right of access so policyholders, claimants, and beneficiaries can learn what ABC Insurance Group holds about them and receive a complete copy within the statutory deadline, even when their data spans policy administration, claims, and document repositories.

subs.title: Confirmation of Processing and Copy of Data with Metadata
subs.description: On a verified request, the data subject receives confirmation of whether their personal data is processed, a copy of that data, and the accompanying processing metadata required by Article 15, including purposes, recipient categories, retention periods, and the source of data not collected from them. Responses must cover all systems holding the individual's records, including imaged correspondence and call recordings, not just the core policy platform.

subs.title: Machine-Assisted Fulfilment Within One Month
subs.description: DSAR fulfilment uses automated identity verification, cross-system data discovery, and redaction tooling so requests complete within the one-month deadline without heroic manual effort. Any extension to the deadline is exceptional, documented, and communicated to the requester within the first month as the regulation permits.

items.name: Right to Data Portability
items.summary: Implements GDPR Article 20 so that data a customer provided to the carrier under consent or contract can move with them, supporting policyholders who switch insurers or aggregate their insurance data elsewhere.

subs.title: Structured, Machine-Readable Export
subs.description: Data the subject provided, such as application details, declared risk information, and account data, is exportable in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format like JSON or CSV. Export tooling produces complete, schema-documented files rather than screen prints or PDFs that defeat reuse.

subs.title: Direct Controller-to-Controller Transmission
subs.description: Where technically feasible, the carrier transmits the portable dataset directly to another controller at the data subject's request, for example to a successor insurer or financial platform. Secure transfer channels and recipient verification apply so portability does not become a data-leakage vector.

items.name: Right to Erasure
items.summary: Implements the GDPR Article 17 right to be forgotten with engineering rigor, ensuring deletion is real and demonstrable across the carrier's full data estate rather than a flag on a single system of record.

subs.title: Verifiable Deletion Across All Stores and Processors
subs.description: When erasure conditions are met and no retention obligation such as statutory claims-record requirements overrides them, the individual's data is deleted from primary databases, backups, caches, logs, and search indexes, and deletion instructions are issued to processors holding copies. Completion is evidenced through deletion certificates or audit records, and backup-restore procedures must re-apply erasures so deleted subjects do not resurrect.

subs.title: Propagation of Erasure and Rectification to Recipients
subs.description: Under Article 19, every recipient to whom the data was disclosed, including reinsurers, TPAs, and analytics vendors, is notified of erasures and rectifications unless doing so proves impossible or disproportionate. The recipient list is drawn from the RoPA, and the data subject is informed of those recipients on request.

items.name: Security of Processing
items.summary: Under GDPR Article 32, technical and organisational measures proportionate to the risk, including encryption, pseudonymisation, and controls assuring confidentiality, integrity, availability, resilience, and the ability to restore data after an incident, are applied to all personal-data processing, and their effectiveness is tested on a regular cycle rather than assumed. Implementation details are governed by the department's Encryption and Application Security standards, which this requirement links to.

items.name: Special Category Data Controls
items.summary: Health, biometric, genetic, and other Article 9 special-category data, which arises routinely in life and disability underwriting and in injury-claim medical evidence, is processed only where a specific Article 9(2) condition applies, with heightened safeguards including restricted access on a strict need-to-know basis and full access logging. Systems holding such data are identified in the data inventory and subject to enhanced monitoring and review.

items.name: Storage Limitation & Retention
items.summary: Operationalizes the GDPR storage-limitation principle so personal data persists only as long as insurance, regulatory, and legal obligations justify, balancing long statutory retention for policies and claims against the prohibition on keeping identifiable data forever.

subs.title: Enforced Per-Category Retention Schedules
subs.description: Retention periods are defined per data category, reflecting obligations such as state insurance record-retention rules and limitation periods for claims litigation, and are implemented as enforced controls in the systems that hold the data. The schedule is owned, versioned, and reconciled against the RoPA so every data category has exactly one authoritative retention rule.

subs.title: Automated Deletion or Anonymisation at End of Retention
subs.description: When a record reaches the end of its retention period, deletion or irreversible anonymisation runs automatically through scheduled jobs rather than depending on manual purge campaigns. Job execution and outcomes are logged so the carrier can evidence that expiry actually triggers disposal, with legal-hold flags as the only sanctioned suspension.

subs.title: No Indefinite Storage of Identifiable Data
subs.description: No system, archive, or analytics store may hold identifiable personal data without an assigned retention period, and lapsed-quote, prospect, and former-policyholder data is a particular focus of periodic sweeps. Data wanted indefinitely for actuarial or trend analysis must first be anonymised to a standard where re-identification is not reasonably possible.

items.name: Transparency & Privacy Notices
items.summary: Ensures individuals receive the GDPR-mandated information about how the carrier uses their data at the right moment and in understandable form, and that the business can prove exactly what each policyholder was told.

subs.title: Article 13/14 Information at or Before Collection
subs.description: Privacy notices delivering the full Article 13 content, or Article 14 content where data comes from third parties such as agents, medical providers, or data brokers, are presented at or before the point of collection in plain, layered language. Quote forms, claims intake, telematics enrollment, and call scripts each surface an appropriate layer of the notice rather than burying it in policy documents.

subs.title: Recording the Served Notice Version
subs.description: The specific version of the privacy notice presented to each data subject is recorded against their record, with notices under version control and dated. This allows the carrier to demonstrate what a given policyholder was told at collection time and to identify which populations must be re-noticed when processing purposes change.

items.name: Data Classification
items.summary: Establishes a uniform four-tier classification scheme so every dataset across ABC Insurance Group's policy, claims, and corporate systems carries a sensitivity level that drives its handling, encryption, and access requirements.

subs.title: Four-Tier Classification of All Data
subs.description: All data is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted at creation or ingestion, with data owners accountable for the assignment. Policyholder PII, claims medical evidence, and payment data fall in the upper tiers, and unclassified data defaults to Confidential treatment until assessed.

subs.title: Enforced Labeling
subs.description: Classification labels are applied through tooling such as document tagging, database metadata, and email sensitivity marks, and downstream controls including DLP, sharing restrictions, and encryption policies act on the label automatically. Labels travel with the data so a Restricted claims file retains its protections when exported or attached.

items.name: Data Masking/Tokenization
items.summary: Prevents sensitive production data from being exposed outside controlled environments by substituting masked or tokenized values wherever the real values are not strictly required.

subs.title: Production Data Masked in Non-Prod Environments
subs.description: Development, test, and training environments may not contain raw production data; refreshes pass through irreversible masking or synthetic-data generation that preserves referential integrity and realistic distributions for testing rating and claims logic. Exceptions require risk acceptance with compensating controls and a defined expiry.

subs.title: Tokenization for Payment Data
subs.description: Card and bank account data used for premium collection and claims disbursement is replaced with tokens from an approved tokenization service, keeping primary account numbers out of carrier systems and shrinking PCI DSS scope. Detokenization is restricted to the payment processing boundary and is fully logged.

items.name: Data Retention & Minimization
items.summary: Limits the carrier's data footprint by enforcing defined retention lifetimes and collecting only what business processes genuinely need, reducing both breach blast radius and regulatory exposure across all lines of business.

subs.title: Enforced Retention Policies
subs.description: Approved retention schedules covering policy, claims, underwriting, and corporate records are implemented as automated controls in the systems and archives that hold the data, with disposal executed and logged when periods expire. Legal hold is the only mechanism that suspends disposal, and holds are tracked to release.

subs.title: Data Minimization Principle Applied
subs.description: Collection points, integrations, and reports are designed to capture and propagate only the fields required for their function. Periodic reviews of forms, feeds, and data warehouses identify and remove fields accumulating without a business justification.

subs.title: No Unnecessary PII
subs.description: Personally identifiable information may not be held, copied, or replicated where the use case can be met with anonymized, aggregated, or pseudonymous data, a rule applied with particular force to analytics extracts, reporting marts, and vendor data shares. Discovery scans flag PII appearing outside sanctioned locations for remediation.

items.name: PII/PHI Handling
items.summary: Governs the identification and protection of personally identifiable information and protected health information, which an insurer handling life, disability, and injury claims processes at scale, ensuring every such field is known and cryptographically protected.

subs.title: PII/PHI Fields Identified and Documented
subs.description: Every system's data model is scanned and reviewed to identify fields containing PII or PHI, including names, SSNs, medical diagnoses, and treatment records embedded in claims notes and documents, and the findings are documented in the enterprise data inventory. The inventory is refreshed as schemas change so new sensitive fields cannot enter production undocumented.

subs.title: Encryption, Masking, or Tokenization Required
subs.description: Each documented PII or PHI field must be protected by at least one approved technique, with encryption for storage and transit, masking for display and non-production use, or tokenization for high-value identifiers, chosen according to the field's classification and use. Storing such fields in plaintext, including in logs and extracts, is a standards violation subject to remediation tracking.

items.name: Secure Data Transfer
items.summary: Sensitive data leaving a system boundary, whether bordereaux to reinsurers, eligibility files to group-benefits clients, or medical records to TPAs, must move only over approved secure channels: SFTP, encrypted email, or a sanctioned managed file transfer service. Ad hoc methods such as unencrypted email attachments, consumer file-sharing sites, and removable media are prohibited, and DLP controls monitor for circumvention.

items.name: Certificate Management
items.summary: Governs the lifecycle of PKI certificates protecting the carrier's websites, agent portals, APIs, and internal services, preventing both cryptographic weakness and the outages caused by unmanaged expiry.

subs.title: Minimum 2048-Bit RSA Key Strength
subs.description: Certificates issued or renewed for any ABC Insurance Group system must use RSA keys of 2048 bits or greater, or an approved equivalent-strength algorithm. Weaker certificates discovered in inventory scans, including on legacy policy-administration interfaces and vendor-managed endpoints, are scheduled for replacement.

subs.title: Annual Certificate Rotation
subs.description: Every certificate is rotated at least annually, with renewals tracked in a central certificate inventory and automated where the platform supports it. Expiry alerting begins well ahead of the rotation date so customer portals and B2B integrations with agencies and reinsurers do not fail on a lapsed certificate.

items.name: Encryption at Rest Standard
items.summary: Sets the baseline cryptographic protection for stored data across the carrier's databases, file stores, and backups, so that loss of media or storage-layer compromise does not expose policyholder information.

subs.title: AES-256 for All Data at Rest
subs.description: All persisted data, spanning databases, object storage, file shares, backups, and endpoint disks, is encrypted with AES-256 or a stronger approved algorithm. Platform-native encryption is acceptable when it meets the algorithm requirement and its keys are managed under the Key Management Standard.

subs.title: Database TDE for Sensitive Data Stores
subs.description: Transparent Data Encryption is enabled on every database holding Confidential or Restricted data, including policy administration, claims, billing, and data warehouse platforms. TDE status is verified through configuration scanning, and any sensitive store found unencrypted is remediated as a tracked exception.

items.name: Encryption in Transit Standard
items.summary: Defines the minimum transport-layer protection for data moving between systems, ensuring customer, agent, and partner communications with ABC Insurance Group cannot be intercepted or downgraded to insecure protocols.

subs.title: TLS 1.2 Minimum for External Communications
subs.description: Every external connection, including customer and agent portals, public APIs, vendor integrations, and reinsurer data exchanges, must negotiate TLS 1.2 or higher with approved cipher suites. Legacy protocols such as SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1 are disabled at the endpoint, and partner connections that cannot meet the floor require a risk-accepted exception with a remediation date.

subs.title: TLS 1.3 Preferred
subs.description: New services are built to negotiate TLS 1.3 by default, and existing endpoints adopt it as platforms and partners allow. The newer protocol's forward secrecy and reduced handshake exposure make it the target state, with TLS 1.2 retained only for compatibility.

items.name: Key Management Standard
items.summary: Governs how cryptographic keys and secrets are generated, stored, used, and retired across the enterprise, because the carrier's encryption controls are only as strong as the custody of the keys behind them.

subs.title: Keys Managed via Approved KMS/HSM
subs.description: All cryptographic keys are generated and held within an approved key management service or hardware security module, with key custodian roles separated from the administrators of the systems the keys protect. Key usage is logged, and keys never leave the KMS or HSM boundary in plaintext.

subs.title: No Hardcoded Secrets
subs.description: Credentials, API keys, and cryptographic material may not be embedded in source code, configuration files, container images, or CI/CD pipeline definitions; applications retrieve secrets at runtime from an approved vault. Automated repository and image scanning detects hardcoded secrets, which are revoked and rotated on discovery, not merely deleted from the code.

subs.title: Enforced Rotation Policy
subs.description: Keys and secrets rotate on defined schedules appropriate to their type and exposure, with automated rotation wherever the platform supports it and immediate out-of-cycle rotation upon suspected compromise or custodian departure. Rotation compliance is tracked centrally and overdue keys are escalated.

items.name: Access Request & Provisioning SLA
items.summary: Sets the service levels for getting access requests reviewed and accounts provisioned, balancing the productivity of adjusters, underwriters, and service staff against the control requirement that all access is approved before it exists.

subs.title: Access Requests Processed Within 4 Business Hours
subs.description: Submitted access requests receive an approval decision from the entitlement owner or delegate within four business hours. Requests route automatically to the correct approver based on the system and role requested, and aging requests escalate so onboarding adjusters and seasonal claims staff are not left idle awaiting a decision.

subs.title: Provisioning Within 24 Hours
subs.description: Approved access is technically provisioned within 24 hours, through automated joiner-mover workflows where integration exists and tracked manual fulfillment elsewhere. Provisioning actions are logged against the originating request so every active entitlement traces to an approval, and SLA performance is reported to IAM governance.

items.name: Break-Glass Procedures
items.summary: Documented emergency access procedures allow authorized staff to obtain elevated access during outages or incidents, such as restoring a down claims platform during a catastrophe event, but only with dual approval and a mandatory, tamper-evident audit trail of every action taken. Break-glass credentials are sealed, monitored for use, rotated after each invocation, and every use triggers a post-incident review.

items.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
items.summary: Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all external access including remote workforce, agent, and broker connections, for every privileged account, and for sensitive systems such as claims payment, policy administration, and HR platforms. Phishing-resistant factors are preferred, SMS-only fallback is restricted, and MFA enrollment is enforced at account creation so no in-scope account operates on a password alone.

items.name: Privileged Access Management (PAM)
items.summary: Places all administrative and elevated access under the control of a PAM platform, eliminating standing privileged credentials and making every administrative action on the carrier's systems attributable and reviewable.

subs.title: All Privileged Access via PAM Tool
subs.description: Administrative access to servers, databases, network devices, and cloud consoles is brokered exclusively through the approved PAM platform, which vaults and rotates the underlying credentials. Direct use of shared or local admin accounts outside the tool is prohibited and monitored, including for vendors administering hosted insurance platforms.

subs.title: Just-in-Time Access
subs.description: Privileged entitlements are granted on demand for a defined task and time window rather than held permanently, with elevation requests approved and automatically revoked at expiry. This keeps standing privileged accounts near zero and shrinks the attack surface an intruder can harvest.

subs.title: Session Recording for Admin Activities
subs.description: Privileged sessions launched through the PAM platform are recorded, with keystroke or video capture retained per the retention schedule and protected from alteration by the administrators being recorded. Recordings support incident forensics and are sampled during periodic reviews of high-risk activity such as production database changes.

items.name: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
items.summary: All system access is granted through defined roles rather than individual entitlements, with each role documented as to its purpose, permissions, and owner, and with periodic access reviews certifying that assignments remain appropriate. Role design enforces least privilege and segregation of duties, for example separating claims adjudication from claims payment release, and review-identified excess access is revoked within defined timelines.

items.name: Service Account Management
items.summary: Every service account is inventoried with a documented purpose and accountable owner, configured as non-interactive so humans cannot log in with it, scoped to least privilege for its specific integration or batch function, and subject to automated password or key rotation. Interactive use of a service account, common in legacy batch processing for policy and billing cycles, is detected and treated as a security event.

items.name: Forensics Readiness
items.summary: Ensures the carrier can investigate security incidents to an evidentiary standard, preserving the artifacts needed for root-cause analysis, regulatory notifications, litigation, and law-enforcement referral.

subs.title: Documented Forensic Tools and Procedures
subs.description: Approved forensic tooling for disk, memory, log, and cloud-artifact acquisition is maintained in a ready state, and step-by-step procedures cover acquisition, chain of custody, and analysis. Designated responders are trained on the procedures, and engagement terms with an external forensics firm are pre-established for incidents exceeding internal capacity.

subs.title: Evidence Preservation Within 1 Hour
subs.description: Once an incident is declared, preservation of volatile and at-risk evidence, including memory captures, relevant logs, and snapshots of affected systems, begins within one hour, before remediation actions can destroy it. Preserved evidence is stored with chain-of-custody documentation so it remains usable for regulatory proceedings and potential claims litigation.

items.name: IR Plan & Escalation
items.summary: Maintains the enterprise incident response plan and its escalation machinery so security events affecting the carrier's operations and policyholder data are classified consistently and reach the right responders and executives without delay.

subs.title: Documented IR Plan with Severity Definitions
subs.description: A maintained incident response plan defines roles, communication paths, decision authority, and the severity classification scheme used to triage every event. The plan addresses insurance-specific scenarios such as claims-data exfiltration and ransomware against policy administration, aligns with breach-notification obligations including the 72-hour NYDFS and GDPR clocks, and is reviewed and updated at least annually.

subs.title: 15-Minute Escalation for Sev1 Incidents
subs.description: Events classified Severity 1 trigger escalation to the incident commander and designated leadership within 15 minutes of classification, through an on-call rotation with automated paging and acknowledgment tracking. Failed acknowledgments escalate automatically up the chain so an active breach never waits on a single unreachable responder.

items.name: Severity Definitions
items.summary: Establishes the enterprise severity scale for security events: Severity 1 for an active breach or data loss, Severity 2 for an attempted breach, Severity 3 for an identified vulnerability, and Severity 4 for an anomaly warranting investigation. Consistent application of these definitions drives escalation timing, executive notification, and regulatory-clock decisions, and triage staff are trained to classify against them rather than by judgment call.

items.name: Tabletop Exercises
items.summary: Validates the incident response capability through a regular exercise program, so plans, contact trees, and decision-making are proven before a real breach of policyholder data tests them.

subs.title: Quarterly Tabletop Exercises
subs.description: Each quarter, a facilitated tabletop walks responders and business stakeholders through a realistic scenario, rotating across threats such as ransomware in the claims environment, vendor compromise at a TPA, and insider data theft. Findings, gaps, and action items are documented and tracked to closure, and scenarios periodically include legal, communications, and the privacy office to rehearse notification decisions.

subs.title: Annual Full IR Simulation
subs.description: Once a year, a full-scope simulation exercises the response end to end, including technical containment actions, executive crisis management, and regulator and customer communication drafting, going beyond discussion to hands-on execution. The simulation tests the 72-hour notification workflow and produces a formal after-action report with plan updates.

items.name: Cloud Security Posture
items.summary: Maintains continuous assurance over the carrier's cloud estate, where policy, claims, and analytics workloads increasingly run, by detecting configuration drift and access sprawl before they become exposures.

subs.title: CSPM Enabled
subs.description: A cloud security posture management platform is deployed across all cloud accounts and subscriptions, continuously evaluating resources against the carrier's hardening baselines and benchmark frameworks. Coverage is verified as new accounts are created so shadow environments cannot escape monitoring.

subs.title: Automated Misconfiguration Detection
subs.description: Misconfigurations such as public storage buckets, open security groups, and unencrypted volumes are detected automatically and routed to owning teams with severity-based remediation deadlines, and the highest-risk findings trigger auto-remediation or alerting in near real time. Findings involving stores of policyholder data are prioritized above the standard SLA.

subs.title: Quarterly IAM Policy Reviews
subs.description: Cloud IAM roles, policies, and trust relationships are reviewed each quarter to remove unused permissions, over-broad wildcard grants, and dormant identities, with particular attention to cross-account access used by vendors and managed-service providers. Review outcomes are documented and permission reductions are tracked to completion.

items.name: Database Hardening
items.summary: Defines the security baseline for the database platforms underpinning policy administration, claims, billing, and analytics, layering encryption, network isolation, and accountability controls on the carrier's most data-dense assets.

subs.title: Database TDE Enabled
subs.description: Transparent Data Encryption is enabled on all database instances in scope, encrypting data files, transaction logs, and backups at the storage layer with keys managed under the Key Management Standard. Compliance is checked through automated configuration scans, and new instances cannot be promoted to production without TDE verified.

subs.title: Restricted Network Access
subs.description: Databases accept connections only from authorized application tiers and administrative jump hosts, enforced through firewall rules, security groups, and private network placement; no database listens on a public interface. Direct workstation-to-database connectivity is limited to approved administrators through controlled paths.

subs.title: Audit Logging Enabled
subs.description: Database audit logging captures privileged operations, schema changes, authentication events, and access to sensitive tables such as policyholder PII and claims medical data. Logs ship to the central SIEM, are protected from modification by database administrators, and are retained per the records schedule to support investigations and regulatory examinations.

items.name: Network Segmentation
items.summary: Divides the carrier's network into controlled zones so that a compromise of one environment, such as a marketing site or agency-facing service, cannot spread laterally into core policy, claims, and payment systems.

subs.title: Documented Firewall Rules
subs.description: Every firewall rule is documented with its business justification, owner, and review date, and rule changes flow through change management with security approval. Periodic recertification removes expired and shadowed rules so the rulebase reflects current data flows rather than accumulated history.

subs.title: Microsegmentation for Sensitive Workloads
subs.description: Workloads processing Restricted data, including claims payment, policy administration, and PII-bearing databases, are isolated with microsegmentation that permits only explicitly defined east-west flows between them. Segmentation policies follow the workload across data center and cloud placement and are validated through periodic traffic analysis and penetration testing.

subs.title: DMZ Required
subs.description: All internet-facing services, including customer portals, agent and broker gateways, and partner file-transfer endpoints, are deployed in a demilitarized zone separated from internal networks by inspected control points. Systems in the DMZ hold no persistent sensitive data and reach internal services only through tightly scoped, monitored connections.
